03 / FIELD GUIDE

From the graph to LMFDB

The LMFDB is a deep catalog of curves over ℚ. Use this map to read the 11.a isogeny class that came up in our earlier discussions.

Explore class 11.a ↗
01 / EQUATION

Which model am I looking at?

LMFDB often shows a minimal general Weierstrass equation with five coefficients [a₁,a₂,a₃,a₄,a₆]. A simplified short equation may have much larger coefficients. Both describe isomorphic curves, but their displayed discriminants can differ by a twelfth power.

See an 11.a curve ↗
02 / INVARIANTS

What do the numbers tell us?

The discriminant detects singularity. The j-invariant classifies the curve over an algebraic closure. The conductor records bad reduction; rank describes the free part of E(ℚ), while torsion records its finite part.

Understand labels ↗
03 / LOCAL TO GLOBAL

Why count modulo primes?

At a prime of good reduction, the number of points over 𝔽ₚ gives aₚ = p + 1 − #E(𝔽ₚ). These coefficients link the curve to its L-function and modular form. A prime dividing the discriminant of a chosen model needs a reduction check.

Inspect the isogeny class ↗
